source.title: Monosemanticity in Recommender Systems
source.authors: Yagel Alfasi; Eden Rzezak; Eadan Schechter

record.tranche_reason: The study measures neuron coherence using an adapted geometric score and LLM-generated labels, and reports a neuron whose label is coherent while its geometric score is low. This refines how monosemanticity should be assessed, but does not test the claim in vision or language models.
record.gate_note: The study applies a geometric monosemanticity score to 50 MSAE latents and separately labels top-activating items. These results bear on V7. The gender-neuron activation interventions report recommendation outcomes, not a rate or score of polysemanticity; they are recorded as findings outside the listed versions. The SAE/MSAE comparison reports recommendation fidelity, not a comparison of their monosemanticity scores.
record.test_reason: The study trains a Matryoshka SAE (50 latents) on 20-dimensional matrix-factorization item embeddings of a recommender. It scores the SAE's own latents for monosemanticity, with hyperparameters tuned to maximize mean MS. It never measures polysemanticity of the network's own units in a vision classifier or language model. It uses superposition and monosemanticity ideas as motivation and tooling, and reports only its own method's interpretability and steering results. The N3 score-versus-label dissociation concerns SAE latents in a recommender, a different kind of system and unit than the versions name, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also claim causal, controllable steering via the gender latents, and that MSAE matches or slightly beats a plain SAE on recommendation fidelity. The paraphrase should add that they frame MS and label coherence as complementary notions of monosemanticity.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an MSAE on recommender-system item embeddings and an adapted item-embedding cosine-similarity score; labels top-activating items with an LLM. It does not reproduce the original vision-neuron method.
record.method_sensitivity: The study explicitly distinguishes geometric coherence measured by the adapted MS score from semantic coherence assessed through LLM-generated labels. It does not vary the activation range used for scoring.

fits_no_version.finding: In an MSAE trained on Amazon Fashion MF item embeddings, latent N3 gets a coherent women's-apparel LLM label yet one of the lowest geometric MS scores (0.076). The authors call MS and label coherence complementary but distinct.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For SAE latents on recommender embeddings, geometric monosemanticity scores and LLM-label coherence can disagree about whether a latent is monosemantic.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling six gender-associated MSAE latents (alpha 1.5 or 0.5) shifts women-associated recommendation share by about 1 point (0.53 to 0.54/0.52), with Overlap@50 of 0.97 and KL about 0.07.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time scaling of selected MSAE latents in an MF recommender modestly shifts recommendation composition while preserving most of the list.

record.problems: The study uses one dataset and domain, a 5,000-item subsample for the MS analysis, and LLM-generated labels without human validation. The authors say the geometric score is indirectly related to human-perceived interpretability. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the MS results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant numeric monosemanticity results are stated beyond the aggregate distribution and named neuron scores recorded. Figure-only intervention response-curve values across scaling factors and category-token changes were not extracted as rows because they do not measure a listed version; the text describes their direction but does not give the underlying values.

untested.parts: All: no vision classifier neurons are examined.
All: no transformer language-model MLP neurons are examined.
All: superposition is invoked only as background; there is no test of the cause of polysemanticity.
All: the SAE vs MSAE comparison reports recommendation fidelity only, and does not report polysemanticity shares of the base model.

All for model neurons. The only related evidence is one SAE latent (N3) in a recommender, where MS and the LLM label disagree. The activation range is not varied, and scoring methods are not systematically compared.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is internally inconsistent. N3 is among the lowest-MS latents and is low-indexed, yet it is in the gender set. The text says the gender axis appears exclusively among higher-indexed neurons and that most selected latents sit at the high end of the MS distribution. Both MSAE and SAE were tuned to maximize mean MS, so MS values are partly selection outcomes. The record's instructions_in_text 'y' appears to refer to the study's own LLM labeling prompts in Appendix A; these are not directed at the reader and were not followed.

versions.untested_parts: Vision classifiers and responses to multiple unrelated image inputs.
Transformer language-model MLP neurons and polysemanticity across layers.
Whether superposition or excess sparse-feature capacity causes polysemanticity.
Polysemanticity from initialization, regularization, or training noise when feature capacity is sufficient.
The study compares SAE and MSAE recommendation fidelity, but does not compare their monosemanticity results or measure changes in the share of polysemantic neurons.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons in vision or language models detect shared features or related jobs.
The study contrasts geometric coherence with LLM-generated label coherence, but does not vary the activation range used or systematically compare explanation-scoring methods.

rows.subject: MSAE on Amazon Fashion MF item embeddings
rows.stage_stated: post-hoc MSAE trained on fixed MF item embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Adapted monosemanticity score: activation-weighted pairwise cosine similarity of highly activating items in MF embedding space
rows.measure: MS distribution across 50 neurons; scores approximately 0.075–0.201, with clusters at 0.08–0.11 and 0.16–0.19; authors characterize the majority as broadly tuned and a smaller group as more specialized
rows.note: Aggregate over the 50 neurons; the paper describes two clusters and interprets the lower-scoring majority as broadly tuned.
rows.check: Measures MS of the study's own MSAE latents, which were tuned to maximize MS, on recommender embeddings. These are not neurons of a vision or language model, so the row is an own-method result rather than a test of V7.

reader_labels.reason: The score and label assessment can diverge: N3 has a women's-apparel label but a low score, and the authors describe the measures as complementary; see r1 and r7.
